subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What scope should OpenClaw accept for this native-VPS performance investigation: a documentation/runbook synthesis, new instrumentation coverage, or a broader optimization program?
rationale: The issue asks for analysis across many runtime layers rather than a single broken contract, so automation needs maintainer-selected measurement environment, accepted evidence, and stop conditions before implementation.

options.title: Runbook First
options.body: Publish a bounded native-Linux performance runbook that uses current diagnostics and identifies explicit instrumentation gaps for separate follow-up work.

options.title: Instrumentation First
options.body: Prioritize new spans around the largest known opaque prep paths, then write the analysis after data is available.

options.title: Fold Into Gateway Pressure Tracker
options.body: Treat this as context for broader Gateway event-loop work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78861 and leave no separate runbook deliverable.

recommendation.title: Runbook First
recommendation.body: Publish a bounded native-Linux performance runbook that uses current diagnostics and identifies explicit instrumentation gaps for separate follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has recent broad history across the current docs, context/model, and runner surfaces and is the best available owner for deciding scope rather than only a single component patch.
